correctness.rationale: A central plane intersects each prism edge when its six endpoint normal heights have opposite signs. The edge graph has six horizontal and three vertical edges. Six great circles of vertex orthogonality have 20 nonzero ordered triple determinants, with absolute rational values 1/2,1,3/2 (times the universal positive factor h sqrt(3)), so their arrangement is combinatorially constant for h>0. Independently enumerated all 64 sign patterns using exact rational determinant signs: precisely 32 nonempty chambers, split 2 six-corner triangular sections, 12 three-corner quadrilateral sections, 6 four-corner quadrilateral sections, and 12 four-corner pentagonal sections; their angle-type signed multisets reproduce the four spherical-excess formulas. The exact spherical areas sum to 4pi; dividing yields P3/P4/P5. Independently checked 20,000 Gaussian normals for each h=0.13,0.5,1,2,5 against the exact probabilities (all deviations <0.01). Differentiating P5 reduces to f(h); f(0)>0, f(infty)<0 and f prime <0 for h>0, giving unique global optimum. The independent root agrees to 12 decimal places. The first-moment edge-angle identity independently checks E[N].

final_claim: For a right regular triangular prism of circumradius-one equilateral base and half-height h>0, a Haar-uniform central plane has 3, 4 or 5 sides almost surely. With S=acos[(h^2-1/2)/(1+h^2)], O=acos[(-h^2-1/2)/(1+h^2)], V=2 atan h, the exact probabilities are P3=3O/pi-2, P4=9-[6(O+S)+3V]/pi, P5=3(O+2S+V)/pi-6. P5 has a unique global maximum at h=0.5314695510636..., the unique positive root of 1+h/sqrt(4h^2+3)=2sqrt(3)h/sqrt(4h^2+1), with maximum P5=0.3851558056742...; E[N]=(6S+3V)/pi.
